sections.h2: Where a Lycoming County deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for property anywhere in Lycoming County are recorded by the Register and Recorder in Williamsport, the county seat. Land records go back to 1795, and every deed from 1795 to today can be viewed online through the searchiqs.com/palyc portal.

The deed is the last paper in a sale. Your buyer's title company or attorney usually carries the signed deed to the recorder after closing, and the recording date is when the public record shows the new owner. Corrections work differently than you might expect: a name cannot be added, removed or changed on an existing deed. A new deed has to be drafted and recorded, and the office points owners to a real estate attorney or title company for that.

Lycoming is the largest Pennsylvania county by land area, about 1,229 square miles, and a house in Jersey Shore, Montoursville or Hughesville is recorded at the same Williamsport counter as one on a city street.

Every instrument that affects real estate needs a Uniform Parcel Identifier, called a UPI, before the Recorder will accept it. That covers deeds, easements, rights of way, mortgages, mortgage assignments, releases, satisfactions and leases, and a 2017 ordinance amendment extended the rule to every instrument involving a specific interest in real estate.

The Land Records Office in the Department of Planning and Community Development assigns or verifies the UPI. It is on the third floor of the Third Street Plaza at 33 West Third Street in Williamsport. The price is $10.00 per UPI, collected when the document is recorded, and a single-UPI document has that charge folded into the base recording fee.

  • Bring or mail the original document to Land Records, or email a draft to upi@lyco.org or fax it to 570-320-2135 for review before closing.
  • Turnaround is roughly 5 to 10 minutes at the counter and no more than one business day.
  • Staff stamp the UPI in the upper left corner of the first page so the Recorder can collect the right fees.
  • One document can list several lots and still need just one UPI.
  • For questions, call 570-320-2130. Weekday hours are 8:30 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon.

If you are splitting off part of a parcel, the new piece is labeled as part of the original UPI, so start the paperwork before the closing date.

The Register and Recorder publishes a fee sheet and updates it from time to time. Get the latest sheet before closing day so your check matches. The base recording fee covers a set number of pages and names, the UPI charge is $10.00 for each parcel identifier, and realty transfer tax is paid on top.

sections.h2: Realty transfer tax on a sale
sections.html:
The commonwealth levies 1 percent of the property's value, and under state law the grantor and the grantee each answer for it. The Williamsport office collects it with the local share and passes the state portion up to Harrisburg.

The recorder's page lists the school districts used for transfer tax purposes, which is the quickest way to see how local tax is split. There are eleven:

  • Canton, East Lycoming and Jersey Shore
  • Loyalsock, Montgomery and Montoursville
  • Muncy, South Williamsport and Williamsport
  • Southern Tioga and Wellsboro, which reach into neighboring Tioga County

A few transfers escape the tax, among them some gifts inside a family, deeds to public bodies and estates passing at death. If you think one of those fits, tell the closing agent early, since the deed must carry supporting language.

If you think the assessment is too high, you can file a yearly appeal from July 1 to September 1, which applies to the following tax year, or file within 40 days after a change of value notice arrives. Each parcel needs its own form. The filing fee is $15.00 for residential property and $50.00 for everything else, including commercial, industrial and Clean and Green.

The appeal has to argue market value. Tax bills and your ability to pay cannot be appealed, and the law presumes the assessment is correct until you show otherwise. The board will not split a property into land and buildings, so the appeal covers total value.

  • Useful evidence: a certified appraisal from the last three years, sales of similar homes within the past three years, photos of a run-down interior and, for rural lots, perc test results.
  • An annual appeal never changes the current year, so keep paying on time.
  • On a change-of-value appeal, pay with a letter saying the tax is paid in protest.
  • A ruling that still looks wrong can go to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days.

Ask the Assessment Office which value will drive the next tax bill, since that is the number a buyer inherits.

sections.h2: Getting the filing right the first time
sections.html:
Most delays come from the parcel identifier, not the deed text. Send a draft to Land Records a few days ahead and ask for the UPI to be stamped on page one. Then confirm the school district and municipality for the property so the transfer tax split is right, check the current fee sheet for the recording amount, and make the check payable as the office instructs. If the sale is a gift or an inheritance, say so on the deed so the exemption language is there when the recorder reviews it.

After recording, keep the recorded copy with your closing papers. It is the proof of when ownership changed, and a corrected name later means a fresh deed and a fresh round of fees.

Lycoming County sits in north central Pennsylvania on the West Branch Susquehanna River. The 2020 census counted 114,188 residents, and owners lived in 67.2 percent of occupied homes. Williamsport is the seat and the only city. The next largest places are South Williamsport, Montoursville, Jersey Shore and Muncy. Lycoming, Loyalsock and Muncy creeks drain the county, so describe flood or creek exposure accurately to buyers if your house sits near one. Cold winters also put roofs and heating systems to a real test, and buyers will ask about both.

faqs.q: Does the Lycoming County recorder fix a misspelled name on an old deed?
faqs.a: Not on the old deed itself. A recorded deed stays as written, and a new deed must be prepared and recorded to add, remove or change a name. A title company or real estate attorney can draft it.

faqs.q: How much is the UPI charge in Lycoming County?
faqs.a: It is $10.00 for each UPI, paid when the document is recorded. A document with one UPI has that charge included in its base fee, and extra UPIs on the same document cost more.

faqs.q: Can I check Lycoming County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. Deeds from 1795 to the present can be viewed online at searchiqs.com/palyc, and the same records can be searched at the recorder's office in Williamsport during business hours.

faqs.q: What deadline applies to a Lycoming County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Yearly appeals go in between July 1 and September 1 and apply to the next tax year. After a change of value notice, the window is 40 days counted from the notice date.

faqs.q: Who covers the realty transfer tax on a Lycoming County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor and grantee each answer for the 1 percent state tax, with local tax added on top. The sales contract normally sets how the two split it, and the recorder collects it at filing.
